feedback: If the child calls a grasshopper nymph a 'larva': 'larva and pupa belong to the butterfly's complete metamorphosis; the grasshopper's gradually-changing young is a nymph — re-tell it with the right word.'
If 'metamorphosis' is used for a puppy or a child growing: 'that is getting bigger, not changing body form — metamorphosis is a change in shape.'
If 'incomplete' is read as 'something went wrong': 'incomplete just means fewer stages and no pupa — the grasshopper is a perfectly complete, finished adult.'
For the frog, confirm: 'the tadpole turning into a frog is a big change in body form — that is metamorphosis too, even though we use the complete/incomplete labels only for insects.'

For the mammal comparison, confirm the terms: 'yes — gestation is the time the baby grows inside the mother, and a puppy or kitten is born with the same basic body form as its parents, so it grows and develops without changing body form the way the butterfly does.'
activities.intendedInsight: 'Metamorphosis' names a change in body FORM, not just size; in insects, complete metamorphosis has four distinct stages including a pupa, while incomplete metamorphosis has a nymph that resembles a small adult and no pupa ('incomplete' means fewer stages, not defective). Metamorphosis also happens in amphibians — a frog changes body form from a gilled, tailed, water-living tadpole into a legged adult with lungs that can live on land — so the word is not insect-only. A live-bearing mammal's cycle such as a dog's or cat's (gestation, birth of offspring, then growth) differs again: precise words let the child compare these kinds of change.
learnerActions: Order the stage cards for a butterfly: egg → larva (caterpillar) → pupa (chrysalis) → adult.
Order the stage cards for a grasshopper: egg → nymph (a small wingless version of the adult) → adult.
Narrate both insect stories aloud using the correct term at each stage, reserving 'larva' and 'pupa' for the butterfly and 'nymph' for the grasshopper.
State which insect cycle is complete metamorphosis and which is incomplete, and say WHY (the pupa/body-rebuild stage is present or absent) — keeping the complete/incomplete labels for insects.

Describe a frog's life cycle to show metamorphosis in an amphibian: egg → tadpole (lives in water, has gills and a tail) → adult frog (has legs and lungs, usually no tail, and can live on land, though many frogs stay in or near water) — a dramatic change in body form, so 'metamorphosis' is not an insect-only word.

Describe a dog’s or cat’s life cycle using gestation, the period the young develop inside the mother before birth, and offspring, the young produced. Compare that selected live-bearing mammal with the butterfly’s larva–pupa–adult transformation; some mammals lay eggs, so do not present live birth as universal.
Sort growth examples into 'changes body form' (metamorphosis) vs 'just gets bigger' (e.g. a kitten becoming a cat) to separate metamorphosis from ordinary growth.
activities.title: Compare life cycles and narrate the change
